headline: Rodrigo Duterte Makes First In-Person Appearance Before ICC
seoTitle: Rodrigo Duterte Makes First In-Person ICC Appearance | FMB News
seoDescription: Former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte appeared in person before the International Criminal Court in The Hague for the first time on September 16, 2026, during a status conference in his crimes-against-humanity case.
deck: The former president attended an ICC status conference in The Hague in person for the first time. The proceeding concerns preparations for his trial, including contested questions about his health and ability to participate.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte appeared in person before the International Criminal Court in The Hague on Wednesday, September 16, marking his first physical appearance in an ICC courtroom.

ABS-CBN News and GMA News independently reported the appearance. GMA reported that Duterte was seated in the courtroom before the judges arrived and, unlike in previous hearings, did not waive his appearance.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: Duterte is detained in The Hague while facing crimes-against-humanity proceedings arising from alleged killings connected with his anti-drug campaign. The allegations are charges before the court and are not presented by FMB News as established guilt.
The ICC has scheduled the opening of trial for November 30, 2026, subject to the court's proceedings concerning Duterte's fitness and ability to participate meaningfully in the trial.

sections.heading: What remains contested
paragraphs: Duterte's defense has argued that his health and cognitive condition affect his fitness to stand trial. Those are defense submissions, not an independent medical conclusion by FMB News. The court is handling the issue through its own legal and expert process.
Duterte has denied wrongdoing and has challenged the ICC's jurisdiction. The ICC has maintained jurisdiction over alleged crimes committed while the Philippines was a state party to the Rome Statute.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The appearance is procedurally significant because it is Duterte's first physical attendance in the ICC courtroom after earlier participation by video. It comes as the case moves toward the scheduled trial phase and as the chamber addresses questions affecting how he can participate in proceedings.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for formal ICC rulings or directions concerning Duterte's fitness, detention and trial preparations, and for any changes to the November 30 trial schedule. FMB News will distinguish court findings from claims made by either the prosecution or defense.

verificationNotes: ABS-CBN News reported and later updated Duterte's first in-person ICC appearance on September 16.
GMA News independently reported the same courtroom appearance and identified it as his first in-person attendance at an ICC hearing.
The article describes crimes-against-humanity allegations as charges and does not state guilt as fact.
Defense assertions concerning Duterte's health are explicitly attributed and are not presented as an FMB News medical assessment.
The hero photograph is the contemporaneous Reuters pool image reproduced in GMA's report; credit and editorial-use status are stated explicitly and FMB News claims no ownership.
